papers.title: Improved osteoblast adhesion and osseointegration on TiO
papers.abstract: To improve initial osteoblast adhesion and subsequent osseointegration, TiO2 nanotubes layer was constructed on the titanium (Ti) surface by anodic oxidation (AO), with an additional hydroxyapatite (HA) coating to form the AO/HA surface. Tests on in vitro cellular activity displayed that the AO surface, especially the AO/HA surface, promoted initial adhesion, proliferation and differentiation of osteoblast cells. The modified AO and AO/HA surfaces further presented an up-regulated gene expression of osteogenic and adhesion markers collagen type 1 (COL), osteopontin (OPN), osteocalcin (OCN) and vinculin. In addition, in vivo experiments with a rat model demonstrated that the AO surface, particularly the AO/HA surface, achieved earlier osseointegration and a superior bone bonding ability compared with Ti. Our study shed light on a synergistic role played by nanotopography and HA in promoting osteoblast adhesion, proliferation, differentiation and osseointegration, thus suggesting a promising method for better modifying the implant surface.

summary_en.motivation: To improve early osseointegration of titanium implants through surface modification.
summary_en.method: TiO2 nanotubes were fabricated on Ti by anodic oxidation, followed by hydroxyapatite coating to create AO/HA surfaces.
summary_en.result: The modified surfaces enhanced osteoblast adhesion, proliferation, differentiation, and gene expression, and in vivo rat model showed earlier osseointegration.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cellular assays and in vivo rat implantation experiments.

papers.title: Variational Adversarial Active Learning
papers.abstract: Active learning aims to develop label-efficient algorithms by sampling the most representative queries to be labeled by an oracle. We describe a pool-based semi-supervised active learning algorithm that implicitly learns this sampling mechanism in an adversarial manner. Unlike conventional active learning algorithms, our approach is task agnostic, i.e., it does not depend on the performance of the task for which we are trying to acquire labeled data. Our method learns a latent space using a variational autoencoder (VAE) and an adversarial network trained to discriminate between unlabeled and labeled data. The mini-max game between the VAE and the adversarial network is played such that while the VAE tries to trick the adversarial network into predicting that all data points are from the labeled pool, the adversarial network learns how to discriminate between dissimilarities in the latent space. We extensively evaluate our method on various image classification and semantic segmentation benchmark datasets and establish a new state of the art on $\text{CIFAR10/100}$, $\text{Caltech-256}$, $\text{ImageNet}$, $\text{Cityscapes}$, and $\text{BDD100K}$. Our results demonstrate that our adversarial approach learns an effective low dimensional latent space in large-scale settings and provides for a computationally efficient sampling method. Our code is available at https://github.com/sinhasam/vaal.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少标注成本，提高样本选择效率
summary_zh.method: 结合变分自编码器和对抗网络学习潜在空间，区分已标注和未标注数据
summary_zh.result: 在多个图像数据集上达到最优性能
summary_zh.validation: 在CIFAR、ImageNet等基准数据集上评估

summary_en.motivation: To develop a label-efficient active learning algorithm that is task-agnostic and reduces annotation cost.
summary_en.method: A variational autoencoder and an adversarial network are trained in a mini-max game to learn a latent space that discriminates between labeled and unlabeled data.
summary_en.result: The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on several image classification and segmentation benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on CIFAR10/100, Caltech-256, ImageNet, Cityscapes, and BDD100K datasets.
